privacyTitle: Built like macOS. Zero root helpers. Zero cloud.
privacySubtitle: Monny is written in pure Swift and SwiftUI on top of Mach, IOKit, and native Apple frameworks. No root daemons, no analytics SDKs, and no server sitting between your Mac and your tools.
privacyRule1Desc: Runs as an ordinary user app — never asks for sudo or installs LaunchDaemons.
privacyRule2Desc: Changes Apple’s built-in macOS 26.4+ charge limit instead of writing raw SMC keys.
privacyRule3Desc: Off by default. When enabled, reads existing local sign-ins directly from your Mac.
privacyRule4Desc: Every release ships with SHA-256 checksums and cryptographically signed updates.

faqSubtitle: Everything about code signing, battery limits, AI provider privacy, and desktop Macs.
faq1Q: Why does macOS show a warning on first launch?
faq1A: Monny is free, open-source software signed with a stable certificate (so macOS preserves permissions across updates), but it is not yet notarized by Apple. On first launch, allow it once in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway, or remove the quarantine flag with xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Monny.app after verifying SHA256SUMS.txt.
faq2Q: How does battery charge limit work without a root helper?
faq2A: On macOS 26.4 and newer, Monny adjusts Apple’s built-in charge-limit setting directly as a standard user — no root helper, kernel extension, or raw SMC writes, and macOS keeps enforcing the limit even after Monny quits. On macOS 15 through 26.3, battery health, cycles, power draw, and temperature monitoring still work read-only.
faq3Q: How does Monny track 22 AI coding tools safely?
faq3A: AI quota tracking is off by default. When you turn it on, Monny reuses each tool’s existing local sign-in and queries provider usage endpoints directly from your Mac (local-only tools like JetBrains AI and Windsurf make no network requests at all). Nothing goes through a third-party proxy, and you can toggle individual tools anytime in Settings.
faq4Q: Does Monny work on Mac Studio, Mac mini, or iMac?
faq4A: Yes. On desktop Macs without a battery, Monny replaces battery-only controls with thermal and fan status while keeping full CPU, memory, disk, network, port search, SMC sensor, and AI quota monitoring.
faq5A: Monny uses Ed25519-signed Sparkle updates so you can review release notes and update in one click (no silent installs), or upgrade through Homebrew with brew upgrade --cask monny.
